Blood samples from a SYNTHETIC vaccine trial travel through a small lab tracking system (LIMS) with a tamper-evident audit trail. An ELISA test measures antibodies, quality checks (QC) decide what can be trusted, and a scorecard checks whether 13 problems we planted on purpose were caught.

Every planted problem was caught
13 of 13
14 of 14 affected records, 9 problem types. Only 1 of 360 samples carried an unexplained flag.
How is this counted?
Almost every vaccinated volunteer responded by Day 29
56 of 58 (96.5%)
Likely range 88.0% to 99.5%. Placebo: 0 of 60.
What counts as "responded"?
Day 29 antibody level: about 19.7 times placebo
4,332 vs 219 AU/mL
Typical level (GMT). Vaccine likely range 3,077 to 6,100, n = 58; placebo 170 to 282, n = 60.
Why both numbers?
2 of 13 plates rejected, both for a planted cause
11 of 13 plates accepted
0 plates rejected without a planted cause. 358 of 360 samples have a reportable result.
Why reject a plate?
The tamper seal broke exactly where we tampered
✗ Broken at row 2,130
On purpose: planted edit to EVT-000924 was found. Rows checked: 2,130 of 6,500; the check stops at the first break.
Is "broken" bad news?

Honesty notes. Both tampers were planted on purpose by generator/tamper.py on SYNTHETIC data. “Tamper on” shows the database exactly as it is now. “Tamper off” for tube SMP-00180 is a clearly labelled replay of the row before the edit; for SMP-00127 it shows the sealed audit rows only. This demonstrates the idea behind an ALCOA+ audit trail; it is not a 21 CFR Part 11 validated system. It detects tampering; it cannot prevent it. A forger who rewrites the row, its audit payload, the chain and the checkpoints would pass every in-database check, and in this demo the external anchor file sits next to the database, so it protects one run only (RISK_REGISTER R-02, KNOWN_ISSUES KI-03).

Before the pipeline ran, the data generator planted 13 problems and wrote them into a hidden answer key: bad lab work, swapped tubes, missing paperwork and two kinds of tampering. The pipeline never sees the key. Afterwards the scorecard compares what the pipeline flagged with the key. Here is each problem in one sentence.

Show
All
Lab bench
Tube identity and custody
Tampering
✓ Caught · P-001

Three of the plate's ruler wells (standards 2, 4 and 6) were pipetted at one-fifth strength. The curve would not fit and the standards read back wrong, so the whole plate was rejected.

Planted as INJ-1 on PLATE-007 · expected flag FIT_FAIL,STD_RECOVERY · raised FIT_FAIL,STD_RECOVERY · Lab bench

✓ Caught · P-002

Two tubes (SMP-00257 and SMP-00281) were swapped in the plate map. The plate map and the LIMS disagreed about which tube was in which well, so both results were held back rather than reported under the wrong person.

Planted as INJ-2 on SMP-00257, SMP-00281 · expected flag ID_MISMATCH · raised ID_MISMATCH · Tube identity and custody

✓ Caught · P-003

A tube's “received” step was never written down. The custody check spotted the gap between “collected” and “aliquoted”.

Planted as INJ-3 on SMP-00164 · expected flag CUSTODY_GAP · raised CUSTODY_GAP · Tube identity and custody

✓ Caught · P-004

A custody step was written down 30 hours after it happened; the limit is 24. It was flagged as a late entry, the “Contemporaneous” part of ALCOA+.

Planted as INJ-4 on EVT-001077 · expected flag LATE_ENTRY · raised LATE_ENTRY · Tube identity and custody

✓ Caught · P-005

The high control read at 1.6 times its target while the curve itself looked fine. The control check rejected the plate.

Planted as INJ-5 on PLATE-003 · expected flag CTRL_OOR · raised CTRL_OOR · Lab bench

✓ Caught · P-006

One of the sample's two duplicate wells read at 45% of the other. The duplicate check (more than 20% disagreement) blocked the result and sent it for re-test.

Planted as INJ-6 on SMP-00050 · expected flag DUP_CV ·

Every dotted-underlined word on this site links here. Hover it, or move to it with the keyboard, for a short definition. Definitions are short on purpose. Each one names its source, and says plainly when there is none yet.

Find a term
33 results

33 of 33 terms.

4PL· Four-parameter logistic curve
An S-shaped line fitted through the standards. It turns the colour reading of a well into an amount of antibody. Its four numbers set the bottom, the top, the middle point and the steepness.
This project's own definition: pipeline/curve.py four_pl(); docs/METRICS.md
ALCOA+· Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate, plus Complete, Consistent, Enduring, Available
A checklist for trustworthy records: who did it, can you read it, was it written at the time, is it the original, is it correct, and is nothing missing.
Standard reference, named but not re-opened for this site: www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/data-
Assay
Any lab test that measures how much of something is in a sample.
Plain-English wording, no external source yet
AU/mL· Arbitrary units per millilitre
The unit for antibody amount in this assay. 'Arbitrary' means it is set by the test's own reference standard, not a physical weight, so it only compares results from the same test.
This project's own definition: config/qc_rules.yaml assay.unit; docs/team/adr (ADR 002)
Audit trail
An automatic, permanent log of who changed a record, when, what changed and why.
Standard reference, named but not re-opened for this site: www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-A/part-11
Blank· Blank well
A well with no sample in it. It shows the background colour of the plate, which is subtracted from every other reading.
This project's own definition: docs/METRICS.md (blank-corrected OD)
Chain of custody
The unbroken record of every hand a sample passed through: collected, received, aliquoted, assayed, stored. A missing step is a gap.
This project's own definition: config/qc_rules.yaml custody.steps

about.html.mainText:
SYNTHETIC DATA
Every volunteer, sample, plate and reading was invented by a seeded generator (seed 42). This is a portfolio demo, not a validated system.
How it works: one command, eight steps, every number traceable
Pipeline diagram, method and honesty notes.
SYNTHETIC
Last pipeline run
2026-10-30 05:19:55 UTC
✓ pytest 245 of 245 passed (2026-10-30)
✓
dbt
 145 of 145 passed
seed 42 · rules QC-RULES-1.0 · build 6b718e9

python -m pipeline.run takes the made-up trial from raw files to this site in about 40 seconds on a laptop. Each step writes to a local DuckDB database, and every change to a lab record goes through an audit trail.

The pipeline
1. Generate
A seeded generator invents 120 volunteers, 360 samples, 13 plate-reader files, and plants 13 problems in a hidden answer key. SYNTHETIC.
2. Load the LIMS
Volunteers, samples and custody steps go into a mini-LIMS. Each insert writes a sealed, hash-chained audit row.
3. Read the plates
Plate-reader files are parsed and fingerprinted. Corrupt files are rejected and logged, not silently skipped.
4. Fit the curves
A 4PL curve per plate from its 8 standards; the valid range (LLOQ to ULOQ) is set from standards that read back within 80–120%.
5. Quality checks
Plate rules (fit, standards, controls, blanks) and sample rules (duplicates, range, identity). A failed plate is rejected whole.
6. Pick one result per sample
The latest run on an accepted plate with no blocking flag. Everything else goes on the re-assay list.
7. Integrity checks
Verify the hash chain, compare every live record with its audit row, check custody gaps and late entries (ALCOA+).
8. Marts and scorecard
dbt builds the report tables and runs 111 data tests; the scorecard compares flags with the answer key.

Then site/build_data.py turns the outputs into small JSON files, and Quarto builds this static site. The browser loads about 0.35 MB of data, with no database.

Method, in brief
Antibody level. ELISA readings (OD) are turned into AU/mL with the plate’s 4PL curve, times the dilution. Results below the LLOQ count as half the LLOQ (22.86 AU/mL) in averages.
Typical level (GMT). A geometric mean with a 95% CI (t-based, on log10 values).
Rise (GMFR). Each volunteer’s later level divided by their Day 1 level, then geometric-averaged. Only volunteers with both results count.
Response (seroresponse). At least a 4-times rise from Day 1 (or at least 4 times the LLOQ if Day 1 was too low to measure), with an exact Clopper-Pearson 95% range.
